I'm working through a list of candidate mentions and deciding how each should be labelled. For the first one, "Duchenne muscular dystrophy" in the murine gene name, I'm weighing whether it points to the gene rather than the disease.

I'm now going through the rest of the candidates. The "Duchenne muscular dystrophy" in "Duchenne muscular dystrophy gene" modifies the noun "gene," so I'll label it as a Modifier. The same reasoning holds for the phrase in "murine Duchenne muscular dystrophy (Dmd) messenger RNA," which I'll also mark as a Modifier. The bare "Dmd" abbreviations name the gene rather than a disease, so they get no label.

I'm now weighing "dystrophic" in "dystrophic mdx mice," since it's a disease-related adjective, but it's a general descriptor rather than a disease name, so I'll leave it unlabelled. The "mdx" strain designation is likewise a mouse strain or mutation name rather than a disease mention, so it gets no label either.

Next I'm weighing "dystrophic mdx mice" against the NONE label I just settled on, checking whether the composite could count as a disease mention. It doesn't. For "human Duchenne muscular dystrophy (DMD) gene expression" the disease name modifies "gene expression", so that's a Modifier, and the abbreviation DMD in the same phrase gets the same label.

I'm settling "mental retardation" as a Disease Class, since the guidelines treat that kind of phenotype term as a condition category. The "DMD" in "some DMD males" is an abbreviation modifying "males," so it gets a Modifier label.
